Executive Summary & Architecture

PayTaxi Ethiopia is a high-throughput, fault-tolerant mobility payment platform engineered for Ethiopian urban transit, including Addis Ababa minibuses (Weyala), Metrolink taxis, and Bajaj networks. The platform eliminates cash-handling friction, prevents payment fraud through animated ticking security receipts, and provides real-time dual-tone audio chime alerts for drivers.

1. Cloud Database Configuration (Supabase PostgreSQL)

The PayTaxi platform uses Supabase PostgreSQL for cloud production. All financial ledgers enforce database-level CHECK constraints preventing invalid transaction states, unauthorized role mutations, or orphaned records.

1.1 Project Specification

Attribute Production Value Technical Note
Project Name paytaxi-db Created under organization heryakos' projects
Project Ref ID sklddyglnuigdnqhegck Unique project identifier in Supabase URL
Cloud Region eu-west-1 (Europe - Ireland / AWS) Matches lowest latency path to Render Frankfurt
Connection Pooler Host aws-0-eu-west-1.pooler.supabase.com Critical: Supavisor IPv4 Pooler (bypasses ISP IPv6 limitations)
Session Pooler Port 5432 Recommended for Prisma ORM schema migrations & transactions
Transaction Pooler Port 6543 PgBouncer transaction mode (requires ?pgbouncer=true)
Pooler Username postgres.sklddyglnuigdnqhegck Format: postgres.[PROJECT-REF]
Figure 2: Creating the paytaxi-db PostgreSQL instance in Supabase Europe Region.

1.2 Critical Architecture Discovery: Direct IPv6 vs. Supavisor IPv4 Pooler

⚠️ The IPv6 Connection Trap & Solution
Supabase direct database endpoints (db.sklddyglnuigdnqhegck.supabase.co:5432) resolve strictly to IPv6 addresses. Most cloud container build environments (including Render, GitHub Actions, and residential ISPs) lack native IPv6 outbound routing. Connecting directly results in Error: P1001: Can't reach database server.

The Solution: Always connect via the Supabase Connection Pooler host: aws-0-eu-west-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432 which provides 100% reliable IPv4 routing.
Figure 3: Supabase Database Settings displaying the Supavisor Pooler configuration and client limits.

2. Code Modifications for Turnkey Cloud Deployment

To ensure seamless interoperability between local development (SQL Server) and cloud production (Supabase PostgreSQL), the codebase was enhanced with driver adapter support and automatic connection string normalization.

2.1 Installing PostgreSQL Driver Adapter

Prisma 7 uses official JavaScript driver adapters. The backend was updated with @prisma/adapter-pg and pg:

cd backend
pnpm add @prisma/adapter-pg pg
pnpm add -D @types/pg

2.2 Dual-Database Abstraction in backend/src/db/prisma.ts

The database singleton was modified to inspect the DATABASE_URL prefix. When running on Supabase, it initializes PrismaPg; when running locally, it defaults to PrismaMssql. 

import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client'
import { PrismaMssql } from '@prisma/adapter-mssql'
import { PrismaPg } from '@prisma/adapter-pg'
import dotenv from 'dotenv'
import { resolve } from 'path'

dotenv.config({ path: resolve(__dirname, '../.env') })

let connectionString = process.env.DATABASE_URL!

// Automatic normalization: if an old IPv6 direct domain is detected, rewrite to IPv4 pooler
if (connectionString && connectionString.includes('db.sklddyglnuigdnqhegck.supabase.co')) {
  connectionString = connectionString
    .replace('postgres:PayTaxi', 'postgres.sklddyglnuigdnqhegck:PayTaxi')
    .replace('db.sklddyglnuigdnqhegck.supabase.co:5432', 'aws-0-eu-west-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432')
    .replace('db.sklddyglnuigdnqhegck.supabase.co', 'aws-0-eu-west-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432')
  if (!connectionString.includes('schema=public')) {
    connectionString += (connectionString.includes('?') ? '&' : '?') + 'schema=public'
  }
}

let _prisma: PrismaClient | null = null

export async function getPrisma(): Promise<PrismaClient> {
  if (_prisma) return _prisma
  if (connectionString && (connectionString.startsWith('postgresql:') || connectionString.startsWith('postgres:'))) {
    const adapter = new PrismaPg({ connectionString })
    _prisma = new PrismaClient({ adapter } as any)
  } else {
    const adapter = new PrismaMssql(connectionString)
    _prisma = new PrismaClient({ adapter } as any)
  }
  return _prisma
}

2.3 Automatic IPv6 to IPv4 Normalization in prisma.config.ts

Render build containers execute pnpm db:push:supabase, which loads prisma.config.ts. The configuration dynamically guarantees that any stale IPv6 direct URL is transparently transformed into the Supabase pooler: 

import { defineConfig } from 'prisma/config'
import { config } from 'dotenv'
import { resolve } from 'path'

config({ path: resolve(__dirname, '.env') })

let dbUrl = process.env.DATABASE_URL || ''
if (dbUrl.includes('db.sklddyglnuigdnqhegck.supabase.co')) {
  dbUrl = dbUrl
    .replace('postgres:PayTaxi', 'postgres.sklddyglnuigdnqhegck:PayTaxi')
    .replace('db.sklddyglnuigdnqhegck.supabase.co:5432', 'aws-0-eu-west-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432')
    .replace('db.sklddyglnuigdnqhegck.supabase.co', 'aws-0-eu-west-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432')
  if (!dbUrl.includes('schema=public')) {
    dbUrl += (dbUrl.includes('?') ? '&' : '?') + 'schema=public'
  }
}

export default defineConfig({
  datasource: {
    url: dbUrl,
  }
})

3. Backend API Deployment (Render Cloud)

The backend is hosted as an active Web Service on Render, deployed from the GitHub repository Heryakos/PayTaxi-Ethiopia on the main branch.

3.1 Infrastructure as Code: render.yaml

services:
  - type: web
    name: paytaxi-api
    runtime: node
    region: frankfurt
    plan: free
    rootDir: backend
    buildCommand: pnpm install && pnpm db:push:supabase && pnpm build
    startCommand: node dist/index.js
    envVars:
      - key: DATABASE_URL
        value: postgresql://postgres.sklddyglnuigdnqhegck:PayTaxi_2026_SecureDb%21%2389@aws-0-eu-west-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432/postgres?schema=public
      - key: JWT_SECRET
        generateValue: true
      - key: NODE_ENV
        value: production
      - key: PORT
        value: "5000"
      - key: FRONTEND_URL
        value: https://paytaxi.vercel.app

4. Frontend (Vercel) & Mobile App (Android APK)

4.1 Vercel Frontend Configuration

The web interface is hosted on Vercel under project paytaxi. The frontend calls the Render backend API over HTTPS.

Figure 7: Vercel Settings -> Environment Variables configuring NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL.
Environment Variable Production Value Scope
NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL https://paytaxi-api.onrender.com Production, Preview, Development

4.2 Standalone Android APK Build (EAS)

To test the mobile app as a standalone Android app outside local Wi-Fi, Expo Application Services (EAS) is configured in mobile/eas.json with a preview profile that outputs an installable .apk file: 

{
  "cli": {
    "version": ">= 12.0.0"
  },
  "build": {
    "preview": {
      "android": {
        "buildType": "apk"
      },
      "env": {
        "EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL": "https://paytaxi-api.onrender.com"
      }
    }
  }
}

Build Execution

cd mobile
eas build -p android --profile preview

EAS cloud servers compile the Android native binary and provide a QR code and download URL. Install the .apk directly on any physical Android device.

5. Comprehensive Troubleshooting & Issue Resolution Matrix

This matrix covers every operational, network, and database issue that may arise in production, along with step-by-step resolution procedures.

Issue 1: Error: P1001: Can't reach database server

Symptom
Render build logs show: Error: P1001: Can't reach database server at db.sklddyglnuigdnqhegck.supabase.co:5432

Root Cause: The database URL is pointing to Supabase's direct hostname, which resolves only to IPv6 addresses. Render build machines do not support outbound IPv6.

Step-by-Step Fix:

  1. Go to Render Dashboard → Web Service paytaxi-api → Environment.
  2. Update DATABASE_URL to use the Supavisor pooler:
    postgresql://postgres.sklddyglnuigdnqhegck:PayTaxi_2026_SecureDb%21%2389@aws-0-eu-west-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432/postgres?schema=public
  3. Click Save Changes.
  4. Go to Deploys → Manual Deploy → Clear build cache & deploy.

Issue 2: FATAL: tenant/user postgres.xxx not found

Symptom
Prisma logs: FATAL: (ENOTFOUND) tenant/user postgres.sklddyglnuigdnqhegck not found

Root Cause: The pooler region hostname does not match the project region (e.g. using aws-0-eu-central-1 instead of aws-0-eu-west-1), or the username is missing the project reference.

Step-by-Step Fix:

  1. Verify the region in Supabase Dashboard → Project Settings → General.
  2. Verify your pooler host is aws-0-eu-west-1.pooler.supabase.com.
  3. Ensure the username format in the connection string is strictly postgres.[project-ref] (e.g. postgres.sklddyglnuigdnqhegck).

Issue 3: Render Free Tier Sleep (50-Second Cold Start Delay)

Symptom
First request from mobile or web takes 50 seconds to respond or times out.

Root Cause: Render Free instances automatically spin down to conserve resources after 15 minutes of inactivity.

Step-by-Step Fix:

  1. Development / Testing: Simply make one request to https://paytaxi-api.onrender.com/health before testing. Once awake, the server responds in <100ms.
  2. Automated Keep-Alive: Set up a free uptime monitor (e.g., UptimeRobot, Cron-Job.org, or GitHub Actions) to ping https://paytaxi-api.onrender.com/health every 10 minutes.
  3. Production: Upgrade Render instance from Free to Starter ($7/month) to disable spin-down completely.

Issue 4: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) Errors on Web Frontend

Symptom
Browser console displays: Access to XMLHttpRequest blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present

Root Cause: The backend's FRONTEND_URL environment variable does not match the Vercel production domain.

Step-by-Step Fix:

  1. Note your exact Vercel frontend URL (e.g. https://paytaxi-ethiopia.vercel.app).
  2. In Render Dashboard → paytaxi-api → Environment, update FRONTEND_URL to match your exact Vercel URL.
  3. Ensure backend/src/index.ts includes your origin in allowedOrigins. Save and redeploy.

Issue 5: Mobile App Cannot Connect Outside Wi-Fi

Symptom
Mobile phone displays: Network request failed when scanning QR code on cellular data (4G/5G).

Root Cause: Mobile app was built pointing to a local LAN IP (e.g. http://192.168.1.3:5000), which is unreachable outside local Wi-Fi.

Step-by-Step Fix:

  1. Verify mobile/.env contains: EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://paytaxi-api.onrender.com.
  2. Rebuild the standalone APK via eas build -p android --profile preview.
  3. Download and install the fresh APK on your phone.

Issue 6: Driver Soundbox Audio Does Not Play in Browser

Symptom
Payment succeeds, but no dual-tone chime or speech announcement plays on the driver's laptop.

Root Cause: Modern browsers enforce strict autoplay policies that block Web Audio API audio synthesis until the user interacts with the page.

Step-by-Step Fix:

  1. On the driver dashboard, ensure the toggle button displays 🔊 Soundbox: Active.
  2. If it displays 🔈 Soundbox: Muted, click it once. The click event grants browser audio permissions and initializes the Web Audio AudioContext.
